title: New ETS: the quick price estimate is linear in the semi-elasticity
why: Q1868 = MAX(Q1860/Q1867,0): the needed relative change of covered emissions (row 1860, from rows 1858-1859) divided by the adjusted semi-elasticity (row 1867 = D1845 x effectiveness row 1866). Emissions respond log-linearly to the price, so the linear estimate misses the cap and is left to the VBA goal seek.
ref: Row 1860 is the change relative to baseline (cap / baseline - 1); D1845 already divides by the volatility ratio D1843, so row 1867 = semi-elasticity x effectiveness x volatility adjustment, as in the prototype. Row 1871 = IFERROR(Q1868,0) catches a reduction of 100% or more (LN of 0 or less).
effect: New ETS scenarios: the quick estimate meets the cap (legacy relies on the VBA goal seek). prototype v0.1.02.
note: The VBA goal seek (ETSMaxIterations, ETSErrorTolerance) still runs from this estimate; no macro change needed.

title: Producer subsidy: other oil products add a per-liter value to a per-barrel price
why: The other-oil-products block is in $/bbl (rows 2681-2690), but its producer-subsidy row reads K$827 (oil producer subsidy, $/liter) unconverted, about 159 times too small. The pre-tax price row 2682 and K2684 (= K2682 - K2683 - K2685) take it as $/bbl; O:AE carry N2685 forward through J2686.
ref: Defined name _conv_barrel_to_liter = Mitigation!E1038 = 158.987294928 ("barrel to liter"), already used in rows 819, 7753, 7786. The other oil blocks (2593, 2616, 2639, 2662) are in $/liter and read K$827 as is.
effect: None for Egypt (row 827 is 0). Otherwise the oil producer subsidy on other oil products is 159 times larger, in $/bbl. prototype v0.6.1 (I49): x LitersPerBbl for a barrel-priced block.
note: No new name needed: legacy has _conv_barrel_to_liter.

title: Blank VAT cells of the price dataset read as a VAT rate of 0
where: Mitigation K772:AE772, K784:AE784, K800:AE800, K805:AE805, K810:AE810, K815:AE815, K820:AE820 (VAT rate rows of the historical price block; VAT_WEO row 726)
why: The VAT rate rows read the IMF price dataset with INDEX(_prices_main, ..., $J); a blank cell returns 0, so a country whose dataset leaves the VAT rate of a household fuel blank gets no VAT on it, although its general VAT rate (row 726, VAT_WEO) applies. Blank cells are missing values, not zeros (an explicit 0 stays 0).
